Writing

A working archive of ideas from the operating side of sport: the questions behind the work, and the conversations that keep moving it forward.

Perspectives

  • Move beyond the next deal

    For decades, sports management has been organized around the next contract, the next sponsorship, and the next season. That rhythm can create activity without creating enough durable value. A stronger approach begins by asking what an asset could become when its talent, story, audience, media, and commercial opportunity are considered together.

    That is the thinking behind a connected sports platform. Advisory creates direction. Marketing gives a property a public life. Media carries the story. Investment gives the right ideas room to compound. The work is to connect those pieces early enough that a partnership becomes the start of growth rather than the end of a transaction.

  • Build the ecosystem, not just the headline

    A league, franchise, or federation is more than the event that appears on the schedule. It is a system of people and decisions: players who need pathways, coaches who need standards, partners who need a credible reason to participate, and audiences who need a story worth returning to.

    Building the ecosystem means making those relationships visible and useful. Commercial strategy should strengthen the sporting proposition. Performance work should create opportunity beyond one roster. When the parts reinforce each other, a promising idea can move from a boardroom to a field of play and then reach the audience it deserves.

  • Create pathways, not just rosters

    Player development is often described as selection: who is in, who is out, and who gets the next chance. The more meaningful work happens between those moments. It is the structure around a player that makes progress repeatable: coaching, feedback, standards, exposure, and a clear next step.

    That perspective applies across cricket and football. A young team can be competitive while still being built for the future. The responsibility is to hold both ideas at once: pursue performance today, and create a route for emerging talent to move into domestic cricket, higher leagues, and the next level of the game.

  • Back founders with context

    Early-stage investing is not only a decision about capital. It is a decision about whether a founder can find the right context quickly enough: a market that understands the problem, a partner who can open the next door, and a strategy that turns a strong product into a durable company.

    The most useful support is specific. Sharpen the go-to-market plan. Test product-market fit with real conversations. Introduce the team to people who can help it learn, sell, and scale across markets. A check matters; the network and judgment around it can matter just as much.

Field notes

  • The operating detail is the strategy

    Big ambitions become credible when daily choices support them: who owns the next step, how performance is measured, and what the team learns before the next opportunity arrives.

  • Build cultures that outlast seasons

    Sport has always been a way to build something meaningful: create cultures, back people, and chase a vision bigger than a single season.

  • Performance is a pathway

    Development is not a single selection moment. It is the structure around a player: standards, coaching, opportunity, feedback, and a clear next step.

  • Long-term value needs patience

    Cross-border sport rewards people who can hold the commercial horizon and the human one at the same time.
